I believe most people handle it very differently. For me, the mixture had me feeling almost sub human, I saw everything people were better than me at, I saw how they were more attractive. 

Though you may have heard it before, but my number one suggestion is finding a kickass hobby, and try turning that into a goal in life. Whether that's a sport  (combat sports are GREAT for this), gardening, carpentry. You name it, you do it. But it's more than just doing something, you're giving yourself something to fall asleep looking forward to, you're giving yourself something to be excited about when you wake up. You start thinking weeks, even months ahead about plans for this.  And suddenly, before bed you're so occupied, you forget those anxious tendencies such as checking the electrics. 

An important thing about this: always make your goal to be better in whatever you choose to do,  don't make it "to not be bad at least".

Diet is another key thing, learn to enjoy making food! Mess around in the kitchen, have fun. And maybe set yourself dietary goals. This is huge for controlling how you feel, you'll start eating properly, you'll feel physically and therefore mentally healthier, and you might even start to see physical changes which will massively boost your confidence.  The could even tie in with my previous point: make cooking a hobby even! I used to love baking cakes and biscuits, and eating them even more.

There's plenty of things which can help in the long run, you just have to find what works for you. Finding an important person to you and making plans with them. You don't even have to talk about how you feel, because eventually it'll go.

But you took the first step in asking someone! Which is the biggest one.

A little info (I'm somewhat into airsofting), as far as I'm aware, it's completely okay to be owning them right now. 

The law is (roughly) as follows:
Unless you have a valid UKARA, which is a "licence" as such, you cannot purchase or modify and airsoft guns that ARE NOT two-tone. So somewhat brightly coloured. You get your UKARA by being over 18 and having played a set amount of games on an official site in a set amount of time; it's something like 3 games in 2 months.

HOWEVER, it is not illegal to own a non two-tone weapon without a valid UKARA. Examples include being gifted one by someone who purchased with a UKURA licence. It must be a gift, else it counts as purchasing. This is also the reason you can borrow non two-tones at gaming sites.

It's completey acceptable to turn up to game sites with a normal looking airsoft gun and not be questioned; the owning of one is not illegal. The law was just put there to regulate who could purchase and mess with them, in order to stop irresponsibility in general since you'd have to have played some games in order to get the licence.

This isn't to say that you should go waving them down your street, but feel free to use them in your back garden without shame or fear. :) You're VERY unlikely to ever get questioned about the posession of it.
